correctness.rationale: The greedy arch index equals the all-target subsequence index by earliest-occurrence induction. Summing arch-length excess and residual length gives 2(n-k); their signed height increments sum to zero, so positive total variation is n-k. A positive 0-run arch rises at most one above its endpoint, yielding H<=n-k+1. If H<=2, arch boundary heights remain 0/1; the only positive-excess arch is a unique 001, with preceding 01 arches and following 01/10 arches and terminal 1. Exhaustive n<=12 Dyck checks and direct target-subsequence tests n<=8 pass; they corroborate rather than establish the infinite assertion.

value.rationale: The maximal nesting height is a canonical complexity parameter of Dyck words, while subsequence universality is a canonical formal-language invariant. Their sharp all-n relation and first nontrivial near-optimal class, including an exact binary-choice normal form and exponential rarity among Catalan words, give a motivated classification beyond routine enumeration or an arbitrary finite case.
